subject.title: [Bug]: Slack Socket Mode ghost connections after gateway restart silently drop inbound messages

question: Should Slack Socket Mode remain warning-only for multiple active connections, or should OpenClaw add plugin-owned recovery/fencing behavior for stale same-gateway restart ghosts?
rationale: Slack documents multiple active Socket Mode connections as a valid pattern, while this issue reports a single-gateway restart state that silently loses inbound messages; automation cannot choose the compatibility policy or false-positive tolerance without maintainer intent and live Slack proof.

options.title: Live-proof targeted recovery
options.body: Require a live Slack restart reproduction, then implement a Slack-plugin recovery path that targets stale same-gateway restart ghosts without breaking documented active-active deployments.

options.title: Keep warning-only policy
options.body: Treat the current warning, relay guidance, and HTTP guidance as the supported behavior, accepting the manual stop-wait-start workaround until stronger proof appears.

options.title: Prefer relay or HTTP for production
options.body: Clarify that production multi-gateway or zero-loss Slack deployments should use relay or HTTP Request URLs instead of adding more Socket Mode recovery policy.

recommendation.title: Live-proof targeted recovery
recommendation.body: Require a live Slack restart reproduction, then implement a Slack-plugin recovery path that targets stale same-gateway restart ghosts without breaking documented active-active deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: The history search shows the broadest recent overlap across Slack reconnect diagnostics and gateway health policy, making this the best available routing owner for the product-policy choice.
